messages.author: b5f242e7eb90c7c9
messages.subject: About some common Rasch indices
parts:
Dear all,

I am pretty new to IRT and I wonder if MIRT or any other R packages provide the following information. I am reading a paper using Rasch analysis and they provide the following information:

infit and outfit mean square (I believe MIRT does this calculation)
Rasch's principal component analysis (PCA) - conducting PCA on item variance unexplained by Rasch
person separation index
item separation index
Wright map

I know that the information above can be done in the software Winsteps, but I do not know if any R packages do those.

In addition, if I specify a two-dimensional model in MIRT, what fit indices inform me the adequacy of this model? Is it RMSEA? I am familiar with SEM (e.g., TLI, CFI, RMSEA, SRMR) but I am pretty new to Rasch.

Thank you in advance!

Best regards,
Chester

parts:
On Tue, Jun 27, 2017 at 3:19 AM, <chest...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear all,

I am pretty new to IRT and I wonder if MIRT or any other R packages provide the following information. I am reading a paper using Rasch analysis and they provide the following information:

infit and outfit mean square (I believe MIRT does this calculation)
Rasch's principal component analysis (PCA) - conducting PCA on item variance unexplained by Rasch
person separation index
item separation index
Wright map

mirt isn't really a Rasch program per say, but it contains all the components to be. AFAIK only the first in your list is supported, the rest would have to be programmed from secondary output functions in the package (e.g., probrace(), fscores(), etc).

I know that the information above can be done in the software Winsteps, but I do not know if any R packages do those.

In addition, if I specify a two-dimensional model in MIRT, what fit indices inform me the adequacy of this model? Is it RMSEA? I am familiar with SEM (e.g., TLI, CFI, RMSEA, SRMR) but I am pretty new to Rasch.

See the M2() function and the associated reference in the help file.

Phil

Thank you in advance!

Best regards,
Chester
